messages:
leah: Heads-up: we need a compact GA checklist for 'Inference Lane'—ops, pricing, and quota mappings. Execs want a one-pager that sales can share. Can we get a short decision thread here?
arthur: I'll start with SLA targets. My suggestion: Hosted: 99.95% uptime, p99 gen <= 300ms (typical 128 tokens). Dedicated: contractual throughput + p99 provide best-effort < 250ms but SLA is uptime 99.9 with throughput SLOs.
mike: Agree on hosted numbers but call out "sequence-size caveat" prominently. For long sequences (>1024) latency p99 can jump; we should state a separate expected tail and offer guidance: use lower-temp sampling or chunking.
sre-bot: Canary policy: must pass 10m of steady-state probes with p95 < 200ms and error rate < 0.1% before GA release. Add rollback triggers: >2x error rate baseline OR p99 increase >50% for 10m.
leah: Good. We also need a precise quota-to-tier mapping for docs and billing. Draft proposal: free/dev = 20 rps, standard = 60 rps (burst 300), premium = 200 rps sustained, dedicated = contract values. Should we also gate concurrent generation contexts?
sara-sales: Sales prefers simple language: "Standard" = production-ready with email support (24 business hours), "Premium" = 1-hour response + phone escalation. We should avoid exposing p99 thresholds in sales blurb but include an appendix link for technical customers.
arthur: On the billing side: map quotas to pricing bands. We should provide an "overage" fallback: soft-throttle at 1.2x quota, then hard reject at 1.5x with clear error code and billing message. Also publish example monthly costs for 500k / 2M / 10M tokens. Mike, can FinOps prepare a sample?
mike: I'll run the token-cost sims. I'll also include a "premium add-on" line item for dedicated fallback model routing and faster support.
leah: Runbook checklist for GA: incident severity matrix, notification flow, required dashboards (p50/p90/p99, errors, TPS, tokens/min), alert thresholds, canary steps, rollout rollback steps, and a short customer-facing troubleshooting FAQ. Elena from docs volunteered earlier; who on SRE owns the alert thresholds?
sre-bot: Suggestion: severity mapping: S1 (service-wide outage) => paging; S2 (significant degradation for >10% customers) => paging + slack incident channel; S3 (single-customer issue) => email ticket. Default alert thresholds: p99 increase > 2x baseline for 5m, error rate >0.5% sustained 5m.
arthur: We'll keep thresholds configurable per-customer for Dedicated. Also, add a gated opt-in for "aggressive caching" behavior that may change token accounting. We must mention that in billing docs.
sara-sales: For the one-pager: I'll write the customer-friendly bits. Leah, can you validate the wording aligns with SLA legal team?
leah: Yes, I'll run the wording by legal and get final copy.
mike: Action items: Mike -> cost sims + sample price bands by Tue; Arthur -> canonical SLO YAML and alert threshold table; Leah -> public SLA wording + one-pager; SRE -> finalize canary commands and add to runbook; Sara -> draft sales blurb + appendix link. Backstop deadline Fri COB.
sre-bot: Health-check snippet to include in runbook: ```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/healthcheck \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"probe":"gen","seq_len":128,"model":"rwd-std-1"}'
```
leah: Thanks, adding that to the runbook. Quick sync tomorrow 10:00 for 20m to confirm the one-pager content. /remind #product tomorrow 09:45 "Inference Lane GA: finalize SLA one-pager"
sara-sales: :thumbsup: I'll prep the customer email template after the sync.
leah: Anything else? If not, closing thread and will ping PRs when drafts land.
